title: Secondary school teacher salary: Award rates, casual loading and super explained
description: Understand the secondary school teacher salary under the Educational Services (Teachers) Award, including hourly rates, casual loading, and super paid on top. Use our timesheet to
salarySummary: A secondary school teacher under the Educational Services (Teachers) Award earns between $38.30 and $52.99 per hour (based on a 38-hour week), with superannuation paid on top of the base rate.

faqs.q: What is the hourly rate for a secondary school teacher under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Educational Services (Teachers) Award 2020, a full-time secondary school teacher in a preschool or school is paid at one of five classification levels. From 1 July 2026, the minimum hourly rates are: Level 1 $38.30, Level 2 $41.86, Level 3 $45.57, Level 4 $49.28, and Level 5 $52.99. These rates are for a 38-hour ordinary working week. The annual salary is calculated as the hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours and 52 weeks. For example, Level 1 equates to $75,941 per year.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to teacher pay?
faqs.a: Casual teachers receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. Under the award, a casual employee engaged for less than five consecutive days is paid no higher than the Level 3 rate. The casual daily rate is calculated as the weekly rate divided by 5, plus 25%. For a full day, this works out to the base hourly rate plus 25% loading. Always use the base rate (without loading) when entering your hourly rate into a calculator, then tick the casual loading box.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For example, if your base hourly rate is $38.30, your employer must contribute an additional 12% (about $4.60 per hour) to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost to the employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Secondary school teacher salary under the Educational Services (Teachers) Award

If you are a secondary school teacher in Australia, your minimum pay is set by the **Educational Services (Teachers) Award 2020** (MA000077), which covers teachers in preschools, schools, and long day care centres. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes the official pay guide, and the rates are updated each year on 1 July. For the 2026–27 financial year, the award provides five classification levels for teachers in preschools and schools, ranging from a graduate teacher (Level 1) to a highly accomplished or lead teacher (Level 5).

### Award rates for secondary school teachers (preschools and schools)

| Classification | Minimum weekly rate | Minimum hourly rate | Annual salary (38-hour week) |
|----------------|-------------------|-------------------|-----------------------------|
| Level 1 | $1,455.40 | $38.30 | $75,941 |
| Level 2 | $1,590.70 | $41.86 | $83,004 |
| Level 3 | $1,731.70 | $45.57 | $90,362 |
| Level 4 | $1,872.70 | $49.28 | $97,720 |
| Level 5 | $2,013.70 | $52.99 | $105,076 |

These figures come directly from the pay guide and the consolidated award. A full-time teacher works an average of 38 ordinary hours per week. Part-time teachers are paid pro-rata at the same hourly rate.

### How to convert your hourly rate to annual salary

The standard formula used on this site is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time secondary school teacher, we assume 38 hours per week. So a Level 1 teacher earning $38.30 per hour would have an annual salary of $38.30 × 38 × 52 = $75,941, matching the award. You can also calculate your fortnightly pay by multiplying your weekly rate by 2. For example, the weekly rate for Level 1 is $1,455.40, so a fortnightly pay would be $2,910.80 before tax and super.

Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see your estimated annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. If you are a casual teacher, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top.

### Casual loading and superannuation paid on top

Casual teachers receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. Under the award, a casual employee engaged for less than five consecutive days is paid no higher than the Level 3 rate. The casual daily rate is calculated as the weekly rate divided by 5, plus 25%. For example, a casual Level 1 teacher would receive $38.30 + 25% = $47.88 per hour (or the applicable daily rate).

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate for 2026–27 is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your base hourly rate is $38.30, your employer must contribute an additional $4.60 per hour to your super fund. The super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### National Minimum Wage vs award rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). The casual rate including 25% loading is $33.05 per hour. However, the Educational Services (Teachers) Award sets higher minimum rates for teachers, so secondary school teachers are always paid above the national minimum. The award rates are the legal minimum; many teachers are covered by enterprise agreements that may offer higher pay.

### Tax and take-home pay

Your take-home pay depends on your total taxable income. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

### Important notes

- The annual pay shown here assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax is based on the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here.
- HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For official pay guides, visit the [pay guides](/blog) page. For more on casual loading, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).
